# Specification: Crew Chatter accounts, auto-saving note editor, dashboard, checklists and responsive app shell

## Context

This is feature 1 of 7 split from `docs/features/crew-chatter/design.md`. It builds on no earlier feature. It turns the existing npm workspaces scaffold into the first working slice of Crew Chatter. That scaffold has three parts:

- The root `package.json` declares the `backend` and `frontend` workspaces.
- `backend` is Express 5 and TypeScript, compiled by `tsc` to `backend/dist`.
- `frontend` is React 19 and Vite 7. Its dev server proxies `/api` to `http://localhost:3000`.

This feature builds only the acceptance criteria listed below. The other six features build the rest.

## Scope

### Backend

- `backend/src/config.ts`: reads runtime configuration (listen port, database location, session secret) from environment variables, with local-development defaults.
- `backend/src/db.ts`: persistence for:
  - users: id, email, password_hash, created_at
  - notes: id, user_id, title, body, created_at, updated_at
  - checklist item completion state
  - password-reset state
- `backend/src/auth.ts`:
  - registration with rejection of an email that is already registered
  - sign-in and session handling
  - password reset request and completion
  - password hashing, so that only a hash is ever persisted
- `backend/src/routes/notes.ts`: create, list, read and update notes, all scoped to the signed-in user. It also provides the "Open tasks" filter and the checklist progress data.
- `backend/src/app.ts`: builds the Express app, mounts the auth and note routes, and installs a final error handler. That handler answers unexpected failures with HTTP 500 and a generic JSON message.
- `backend/src/index.ts`: starts the HTTP listener using `app.ts` and `config.ts`.

### Frontend

- `frontend/src/main.tsx` and `frontend/src/App.tsx`: mount the app and switch between the signed-out auth screen and the signed-in workspace.
- `frontend/src/api.ts`: a typed client for the backend `/api` endpoints.
- `frontend/src/components/AuthScreen.tsx`: register, sign-in, and password-reset request and completion forms, with error messages.
- `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`: left navigation with the "Open tasks" filter. It collapses into a drawer behind a menu button at mobile widths.
- `frontend/src/components/NoteList.tsx`: the note list and the empty state with a create-first-note button. Every note in it can be reached with the keyboard.
- `frontend/src/components/NoteEditor.tsx`:
  - title and rich-text body
  - controls for heading, bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, link, block quote and code block
  - checklist toggling and "N of M complete" progress
  - the save-state indicator
- `frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts`:
  - debounced auto-save with no Save button
  - save-state tracking: Saving, Saved, Unable to save, Offline
  - the beforeunload leave-page guard
  - in-app navigation guarding while a save is pending or in flight
- `frontend/src/styles.css`: the three-pane desktop layout and the single-column mobile layout with a drawer.

The implementation may add runtime dependencies, for example a rich-text editor library or a database driver. Each one must be added to the right workspace `package.json` and recorded in the root `package-lock.json`.

## Verification notes

These notes come from the repository's own files. They describe what the declared artifacts must keep working. They are not acceptance criteria.

- `npm ci` installs from the root `package-lock.json`. That lockfile must match the root, `backend/package.json` and `frontend/package.json` dependency declarations.
- `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` in each workspace:
  - The backend uses `module`/`moduleResolution` `NodeNext` with `rootDir` `src`, so relative imports in `backend/src` need explicit `.js` extensions.
  - The frontend checks `src` and `vite.config.ts` with `Bundler` resolution and `vite/client` types.
- `npm run lint` runs `eslint .` with `@eslint/js` recommended and `typescript-eslint` recommended rules. Files under `frontend/` also get the `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` recommended rules.
- `npm run build` runs `tsc` in `backend`, which writes `backend/dist`, and `vite build` in `frontend`, which writes `frontend/dist`. Both are ignored by the `dist/` entry in `.gitignore`.
- Any database file or other file the app generates at runtime must live somewhere git ignores. `.gitignore` is a declared artifact for that reason.

## Follow-ups already routed during design review

Design review routed these questions as follow-ups. It found that the criteria below can be tested without answering them, so this spec does not decide them:

- how the password-reset token reaches the user (finding 1)
- how long the reset token lasts and whether it can be used only once (findings 26 and 32)
- the exact auto-save debounce interval (finding 12)

The implementation should state the reset mechanism and debounce interval it chooses.

## Out of scope

- Criteria owned by other features:
  - crew-chatter-hardening: AC-004, AC-007, AC-008, AC-009, AC-067, AC-068, AC-076
  - crew-chatter-search: AC-017, AC-035 to AC-040, AC-071
  - crew-chatter-note-lifecycle: AC-019, AC-020, AC-021, AC-028, AC-034, AC-041 to AC-048
  - crew-chatter-folders-tags: AC-022, AC-024 to AC-027, AC-029 to AC-033, AC-073 to AC-075
  - crew-chatter-attachments-versions: AC-052 to AC-059
  - crew-chatter-export-import: AC-060 to AC-063
- Visual tone guidance has nothing to check, so it is not a criterion. This covers the "calm, focused, lightweight" feel, generous line height and restrained formatting controls.

## Declared artifacts

backend/src/config.ts
backend/src/db.ts
backend/src/index.ts

frontend/src/components/NoteList.tsx
frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx
frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts
frontend/src/main.tsx
frontend/src/styles.css

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Registering with an email address not yet in use and a non-empty password creates an account, signs the user in, and displays that user's notes dashboard.
- AC-002: Registering with an email address that is already registered is rejected with an error message and no second account is created.
- AC-003: Signing in with a registered email and its correct password displays that user's dashboard, and signing in with an incorrect password displays an error message and leaves the user signed out.
- AC-005: After a password reset is requested for a registered email and completed with a new password, signing in with the new password succeeds and signing in with the old password fails.
- AC-006: The persisted user record stores the password only as a hash in its password hash field, and no persisted field contains the submitted plaintext password.
- AC-010: Clicking the "New note" button on the dashboard creates a note and opens it in the editor with keyboard focus in the title or body field.
- AC-011: The editor provides controls for heading, bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, link, block quote, and code block, and content formatted with each control keeps that formatting after the page is reloaded.
- AC-012: The editor has no Save button, and an edit to the title or body is persisted with no manual save action once typing stops, so that after the indicator shows "Saved" a page reload shows the edit.
- AC-013: The save-state indicator shows "Saving" while a save request is in flight, "Saved" after it succeeds, "Unable to save" after a save fails while the browser is online, and "Offline" while navigator.onLine is false.
- AC-014: A note whose title and body both contain the text "Crew 日本語 émoji 🎉 العربية" displays that exact text in both fields after it is saved and the page is reloaded.
- AC-015: Pasting text/plain or text/html clipboard content into the note body inserts the pasted text into the body and the note saves it.
- AC-016: Closing or reloading the tab while a save is pending or in flight triggers the browser's leave-page confirmation, and closing or reloading the tab with no pending save does not.
- AC-018: Every note records a creation timestamp and a last-updated timestamp, and saving an edit changes the last-updated timestamp while leaving the creation timestamp unchanged.
- AC-023: When the signed-in user has no notes, the dashboard displays an empty-state message and a button that creates the user's first note when clicked.
- AC-049: The editor can insert a checklist item into a note, and toggling an item's checkbox in the editor marks it complete or incomplete, and that state persists after the page is reloaded.
- AC-050: The "Open tasks" filter lists every note with at least one incomplete checklist item and excludes notes whose checklist items are all complete and notes with no checklist items.
- AC-051: A note with checklist items displays progress in the form "N of M complete", where M is its number of checklist items and N is the number marked complete.
- AC-064: At a 1280×800 viewport the app shows the left navigation sidebar, the note list, and the editor panel side by side.
- AC-065: At a 375×667 viewport the navigation sidebar is hidden behind a menu button that opens it as a drawer, and an opened note's editor spans the full viewport width.
- AC-066: Using only the keyboard, the user can move through every note in the note list and open any of them in the editor.
- AC-069: When a backend request handler fails unexpectedly, the API responds with HTTP 500 and a JSON body whose message contains no stack trace, file path, or database query text.
- AC-070: With the backend running on the same machine as the browser, the editor appears within 200 ms of clicking "New note".
- AC-072: While a save is pending or in flight, navigating within the app to another note or view either completes the save before the switch takes effect or asks the user to confirm leaving, so the pending edit is never silently lost.
- AC-077: With the backend running on the same machine as the browser, typed text appears in the note editor within 200 ms of each keystroke.

- `backend/src/app.ts`: builds the Express app, mounts the auth and note routes, and installs the final error handler for unexpected failures.
- `backend/src/index.ts`: starts the HTTP listener using `app.ts` and `config.ts`.

### Frontend

- `frontend/src/main.tsx` and `frontend/src/App.tsx`: mount the app and switch between the signed-out auth screen and the signed-in workspace.
- `frontend/src/api.ts`: a typed client for the backend `/api` endpoints.
- `frontend/src/components/AuthScreen.tsx`: register, sign-in, and password-reset request and completion forms, with their error messages.
- `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`: left navigation with the "Open tasks" filter. At mobile widths it sits in a drawer opened by a menu button.
- `frontend/src/components/NoteList.tsx`: the dashboard note list with the "New note" button, and the empty state with its create-first-note button.
- `frontend/src/components/NoteEditor.tsx`:
  - title and rich-text body
  - formatting controls
  - checklist toggling and "N of M complete" progress
  - the save-state indicator
- `frontend/src/hooks/useAutoSave.ts`:
  - auto-save with no Save button
  - save-state tracking
  - the leave-page guard
  - guarding in-app navigation while a save is pending or in flight
- `frontend/src/styles.css`: the desktop three-pane layout and the mobile layout with the drawer.

The implementation may add runtime dependencies, for example a rich-text editor library or a database driver. Each one goes in the right workspace `package.json` and is recorded in the root `package-lock.json`.

## Verification notes

These notes come from the repository's own files. They describe what the declared artifacts must keep working. They are not acceptance criteria.

- `npm ci` installs from the root `package-lock.json`. That lockfile must match the dependency declarations in the root, `backend/package.json` and `frontend/package.json`. `npm ci` also runs the install scripts of every dependency, so any added dependency with a native build step must install successfully in the verification checkout.
- `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` in each workspace:
  - The backend uses `module`/`moduleResolution` `NodeNext` with `rootDir` `src`, so relative imports in `backend/src` need explicit `.js` extensions.
  - The frontend checks `src` and `vite.config.ts` with `Bundler` resolution and `vite/client` types.
- `npm run lint` runs `eslint .` from the root. It applies the `@eslint/js` recommended and `typescript-eslint` recommended rules everywhere. Files under `frontend/` also get the `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` recommended rules.
- `npm run build` runs `tsc` in `backend`, which writes `backend/dist`, and `vite build` in `frontend`, which writes `frontend/dist`. Both are ignored by the `dist/` entry in `.gitignore`.
- None of these commands starts the app. `.gitignore` is declared because the split lists it among the files this feature changes, not because a command requires it.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Registering with an email address not yet in use and a non-empty password creates an account, signs the user in, and displays that user's notes dashboard.
- AC-002: Registering with an email address that is already registered is rejected with an error message and no second account is created.
- AC-003: Signing in with a registered email and its correct password displays that user's dashboard, and signing in with an incorrect password displays an error message and leaves the user signed out.
- AC-005: After a password reset is requested for a registered email and completed with a new password, signing in with the new password succeeds and signing in with the old password fails.
- AC-006: The persisted user record stores the password only as a hash in its password hash field, and no persisted field contains the submitted plaintext password.
- AC-010: Clicking the "New note" button on the dashboard creates a note and opens it in the editor with keyboard focus in the title or body field.
- AC-011: The editor provides controls for heading, bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, link, block quote, and code block, and content formatted with each control keeps that formatting after the page is reloaded.
- AC-012: The editor has no Save button, and an edit to the title or body is persisted with no manual save action once typing stops, so that after the indicator shows "Saved" a page reload shows the edit.
- AC-013: The save-state indicator shows "Saving" while a save request is in flight, "Saved" after it succeeds, "Unable to save" after a save fails while the browser is online, and "Offline" while navigator.onLine is false.
- AC-014: A note whose title and body both contain the text "Crew 日本語 émoji 🎉 العربية" displays that exact text in both fields after it is saved and the page is reloaded.
- AC-015: Pasting text/plain or text/html clipboard content into the note body inserts the pasted text into the body and the note saves it.
- AC-016: Closing or reloading the tab while a save is pending or in flight triggers the browser's leave-page confirmation, and closing or reloading the tab with no pending save does not.
- AC-018: Every note records a creation timestamp and a last-updated timestamp, and saving an edit changes the last-updated timestamp while leaving the creation timestamp unchanged.
- AC-023: When the signed-in user has no notes, the dashboard displays an empty-state message and a button that creates the user's first note when clicked.
- AC-049: The editor can insert a checklist item into a note, and toggling an item's checkbox in the editor marks it complete or incomplete, and that state persists after the page is reloaded.
- AC-050: The "Open tasks" filter lists every note with at least one incomplete checklist item and excludes notes whose checklist items are all complete and notes with no checklist items.
- AC-051: A note with checklist items displays progress in the form "N of M complete", where M is its number of checklist items and N is the number marked complete.
- AC-064: At a 1280×800 viewport the app shows the left navigation sidebar, the note list, and the editor panel side by side.
- AC-065: At a 375×667 viewport the navigation sidebar is hidden behind a menu button that opens it as a drawer, and an opened note's editor spans the full viewport width.
- AC-066: Using only the keyboard, the user can move through every note in the note list and open any of them in the editor.
- AC-069: When a backend request handler fails unexpectedly, the API responds with HTTP 500 and a JSON body whose message contains no stack trace, file path, or database query text.
- AC-070: With the backend running on the same machine as the browser, the editor appears within 200 ms of clicking "New note".
- AC-072: While a save is pending or in flight, navigating within the app to another note or view either completes the save before the switch takes effect or asks the user to confirm leaving, so the pending edit is never silently lost.
- AC-077: With the backend running on the same machine as the browser, typed text appears in the note editor within 200 ms of each keystroke.

- OD-001 (medium): How does the password-reset token reach the user, which AC-005 relies on to complete a reset?
- OD-012 (medium): How long does auto-save wait after typing stops, which AC-012 and AC-072 rely on for the pending-save window?
